The flagship NLI recipe was `query=subject,contains,{town}&publication_year_to=1917`: `subject` is not a published NLI attribute and `publication_year_to` is not a current parameter. NLI drops unrecognised conditions SILENTLY and returns UNFILTERED results, so the recipe returned everything and looked successful. Replaced with documented attributes only, plus an Errors-header rule. Never ship a caveat where a wrong example can be removed instead: a caveat cannot reach a user who never sees an error.

Judge round 2 caught a defect I introduced while fixing round 1: the new privacy section asserted the Privacy Protection Law / Amendment 13 sensitive-data classification and a defamation standing rule with no evidence entry, the same unsourced-statutory-assertion pattern round 1 flagged. Fixed by reframing them as operating rules for the AGENT's own conduct and dropping the classification claims. When you remediate an unsourced legal claim, check you have not written a new one in the fix.

The 50-year IDF/defence figure had no evidence behind it in any cycle. Removed the number entirely rather than substituting an unverified one; the skill now tells the user to get it from the defence archive. Same treatment for the statutory attribution of the 70-year window.

Adding the privacy content flipped the skill from 'clear' to 'regulated' in the legal gate, requiring a Legal notice section and a prepended description clause. Expect this whenever a skill starts stating legal obligations, even correct ones.
